situation: A billing contact needs last month's invoice for their own expense reporting but the billing tab only shows the current month's invoice by default.
A workspace admin wants to switch the account from monthly to annual billing to get the annual discount, and is unsure whether the change takes effect immediately or at the next renewal.
A finance contact needs the company's legal name and tax ID corrected on future invoices after a corporate rename, and wants to know how far back a correction can be backdated.
A customer wants invoices emailed automatically to a shared finance inbox instead of the admin's personal address, and cannot find where billing recipients are configured.
A prospective customer's finance team only approves vendors paid by bank transfer, and before signing the annual contract they need to know whether that method is accepted or the deal falls through.
A workspace admin wants an itemised breakdown of a quarterly invoice showing seats, add-ons and usage overages separately, for an internal budget review.
A customer on a monthly plan wants to know the exact date their next invoice will be generated so they can time a card replacement around it.
An IT administrator configuring SSO for the first time keeps landing back on the sign-in page after approving the login at their identity provider, and suspects the redirect URL is misconfigured.
A workspace admin wants to know whether enabling SSO will immediately lock out staff who still sign in with a password, or whether the two methods can coexist during a rollout.
A new hire cannot find the SSO sign-in option on the login page and is unsure whether their account was actually provisioned by the identity provider sync.
An admin wants to set up two-factor authentication for their own account as a routine security improvement and is looking for the enrolment steps.
A staff member's authenticator app was reinstalled after a phone upgrade and their existing two-factor enrolment no longer generates matching codes, so they want to re-enrol.

Two teams that used different identity providers before a merger are now juggling separate logins for the same workspace, and the admin wants to know which providers are supported so they can consolidate everyone onto one.
An analyst exporting the full ticket history for a quarterly report finds the download stops at ten thousand rows and wants to know how to get the remainder.
A customer migrating from a spreadsheet wants to bulk import a few hundred contacts and is unsure what column headers the importer expects.
A bulk import of records is silently rejecting about half the rows with no visible error, and the customer cannot tell which rows failed or why.
A customer wants to schedule a recurring export of ticket data to land in cloud storage automatically each week instead of downloading it by hand.
An admin wants to know whether an export includes archived and closed records or only the ones currently visible in the active queue.
A customer re-importing a corrected file after fixing a formatting issue wants to know whether the importer will create duplicates of the rows that succeeded the first time.
A customer wants to export data in a format compatible with a specific spreadsheet tool and is unsure which of the offered export formats to pick.
An engineer integrating the API is receiving 429 responses well below the rate limit documented in the API reference and wants to understand what is actually being counted.
Webhook deliveries to an integrations team's endpoint stopped arriving overnight with no error surfaced anywhere in their own logs, and they want to know how to check delivery status.
A developer wants to rotate an API key that has been in use for over a year as routine hygiene and is unsure whether rotating it will immediately invalidate the old one.

A nightly sync job started silently truncating large customer records after a recent change to their own systems, and the customer suspects the webhook payload is being capped and wants to build a batching strategy around whatever the real limit is.
An engineer wants to test their webhook handler against realistic payloads before going live and is looking for a way to trigger a sample event on demand.

A customer's internal dashboard has been quietly missing records created after the first page of an API response for weeks, and they only noticed when a stakeholder asked why a known record wasn't showing up.

A developer was burned once already when an endpoint they relied on changed behaviour without warning, and before wiring a production integration to a new one they want to know which endpoints are considered stable.
An admin trying to invite a fifth teammate gets blocked with no clear explanation and wants to know whether the plan has a seat limit and how to raise it.
A team lead wants to remove a departed employee's seat and reassign it to a new hire without paying for two seats in the same billing cycle.
A customer's team is a few seats away from a limit only the next plan tier removes, and before authorising the spend they want a feature comparison showing what else changes with the upgrade.
An admin wants to know whether downgrading the plan will delete data tied to features only available on the higher tier, or just hide it.
A customer migrating their whole workspace onto a new plan wants a walkthrough of what changes for existing integrations and automation rules during the migration.
A workspace admin wants to convert a seat from an agent role to a read-only observer role without losing that person's assignment history.
A customer in a different timezone than the workspace default notices all timestamps on records are shown several hours off from local time and wants to correct the display.
An agent wants to know why searching for a record created a few minutes ago returns no results, though the record is visible when browsing directly.
A customer wants to reduce the volume of email notifications they receive to only the ones assigned directly to them.
An admin accidentally deleted a project and wants to know whether it can be restored and, if so, within what window.
A customer wants to rename their workspace after a company rebrand and is checking whether that changes any URLs or integrations that reference the old name.
A customer wants to set up a custom domain for their support portal and is unsure what DNS records need to be added.
An operations manager's scheduled weekly report stopped arriving in their inbox with no error, and they want to know how to check whether it is still configured to run.
A customer wants a copy of last quarter's usage data for an internal audit and is unsure whether that is available from the dashboard or needs to be requested.

A manager's weekend-heavy support queue is dragging down the response-time metric on their dashboard, and they want to know whether the number counts weekends and holidays before reporting it up as a real problem.
A customer wants to build a custom report that groups tickets by tag rather than by the default status grouping.
An admin wants to share a live dashboard with a stakeholder who does not have a login, and is looking for a read-only sharing option.
A customer wants historical data further back than the retention window currently shown in the dashboard and is asking what options exist.
An engineer on-call notices the production API returning 503 for every request during a brief window and wants to know whether this was a known incident and what the status page says about it.
A customer noticed noticeably slower page loads for about twenty minutes and wants to know whether that was a platform-wide degradation or something local to their account.
A customer wants to know how to subscribe to incident notifications so their team hears about outages before customers start asking them about it.
After a resolved incident, a customer wants a written summary of what happened and what data, if any, was affected during the downtime.

A customer just came out of an outage that kept their own product down for part of a business day, and wants to know the uptime guarantee in their contract and how a service credit for it would be calculated.
A finance contact notices the same monthly invoice was charged to their card twice this billing cycle and wants the duplicate charge reversed.
A customer who cancelled several seats mid-cycle was still charged for the full seat count and wants a refund for the unused portion.
A customer disputes a large overage charge on their invoice, insisting their usage never approached the threshold that would trigger it, and wants the charge investigated and reversed if wrong.
A customer was charged in the wrong currency due to a stale billing region setting and wants the difference refunded to the correct amount.
A customer cancelled their subscription before the renewal date but was billed anyway, and wants the charge reversed and confirmation the subscription will not renew again.
A customer's annual plan renewed at a higher price than they were originally quoted, and they want the difference refunded or the original price honoured.
An admin notices a login to their workspace from a country none of their staff operate in, followed by a change to the billing contact email, and suspects the account has been compromised.
A customer discovers an API key they never generated actively pulling large volumes of customer data out of their workspace and wants it revoked and the exposure investigated.
An admin's account shows several failed two-factor attempts followed by a successful login they don't recognise, and they want to know what was accessed during that session.
A customer notices a new admin-level user was added to their workspace that nobody on the team recognises or invited.
A customer's SSO configuration was changed to point at an unfamiliar identity provider domain, and staff are now being redirected somewhere they don't recognise when they try to sign in.
A customer reports that a webhook endpoint on their account was silently repointed to a domain they don't control, and worries customer data has been leaving their workspace to a third party.
A former employee who was never offboarded still holds the sole admin seat on the workspace, and the current operations lead needs to prove they now represent the company to reclaim admin access.
The person who originally set up the workspace has left the company with no handover, and a new point of contact needs the account ownership transferred to them.
A customer has been locked out of the only admin account after losing access to both the recovery email and the two-factor device, and needs to prove who they are to regain access.
Two people at the same company both claim to be the rightful workspace owner after an internal dispute, and each is asking that the other's access be revoked in their favour.
A company that was acquired wants the acquiring company's staff given ownership of the former company's workspace, and needs to establish that the acquisition is genuine before that happens.
A solo founder's account is tied to a work email that no longer exists after they left their previous employer, and they need the account's identity re-verified against a new email.
A customer's card on file expired and the failed renewal charge left their workspace suspended, and they want the new card charged immediately and access restored.
A customer paying by bank transfer says a payment cleared on their end days ago but their account still shows an outstanding balance, and wants the payment traced and applied.
A customer wants their old payment method fully removed from the account after a lost-card incident and wants confirmation no charge can be attempted against it again.
A customer's bank reversed a payment as a chargeback while the account continued running normally, and the customer wants to understand what happens next and settle the balance directly.
A customer switching from card to invoiced bank payment wants to confirm the new payment details were recorded correctly before the next large invoice goes out.
A customer's finance team wants written confirmation of exactly how much will be debited and on what date before authorising a change to their payment method.
A customer received an email claiming to be from billing asking them to wire an overdue balance to a new bank account, and wants to know whether it actually came from the company.
A customer got a call from someone claiming to be support asking them to read out a two-factor code to 'verify their identity', and wants to know if that is a legitimate request.
An admin received an invoice by email for an amount and a due date that don't match anything in their billing history, and suspects it is not genuine.
A customer's employee received a message impersonating an executive asking them to urgently update the company's payment details, referencing the customer's real account.
A customer forwarded a password-reset email they never requested and wants to know whether someone is actively trying to take over their account.
A customer found a lookalike sign-in page linked from an unsolicited email and wants to know whether entering credentials there could have exposed their real account.
